exercise.instruction: Write the full program: a class 'Dog' with public std::string name, a constructor Dog(std::string n) that sets name, and a method bark() that prints '<name> says woof'. In main create Dog d("Rex") and call d.bark().
hints: Hint 1: class Dog { public: std::string name; Dog(std::string n) { name = n; } void bark() { std::cout << name << " says woof" << std::endl; } };
Hint 2: In main: Dog d("Rex"); d.bark();

quiz.question: What's easy to forget at the end of a class definition?
What does public: do?
options: Makes members accessible from outside the class
